newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilders dip ahead of Easter break.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilders dip ahead of Easter break.

text.p: Overnight guilders dipped on Thursday as the Dutch money market wound down ahead of the long Easter weekend.
Call money dipped to 3.00 percent bid from Wednesday's 3.06 percent as the month-end effect ebbed out of the market, dealers said.
"Most players have covered themselves for the month-end liquidity squeeze and today's special advances allocation appears to have been ample," a dealer said.
The Dutch central bank said earlier it allocated 3.05 billion guilders to the money market under an eight-day pact.
Individual banks' applications up to 3.50 billion guilders were met for 12 percent, with no subscriptions awarded above that amount.
Dealers said activity was concentrated on the short end up to two months, with little action in longer-dated deposits.
There was little demand for Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) despite a lowering of the price, one dealer said.
The DTC programme ending May 30 was priced at 3.09 percent, while the December programme was priced at 3.25 percent.
The guilder remained soft against the mark, quoted at 112.50 per 100 marks, unchanged from Wednesday's fixing.
The Dutch money market will be closed tomorrow, Good Friday, and on March 31, Easter Monday.
